items.stem: A team wants to rebrand a 30-slide deck's colours and logo in one change. What is the right tool?

options.text: Edit the slide master and layouts so every slide inherits the change
options.rationale: Correct: the master propagates branding to all slides.
Per-slide edits are slow and inconsistent.

options.text: Export to PDF and edit there
options.rationale: PDF editing does not update the deck.

options.text: Start a brand-new file for every change

items.explanation: Correct: the master propagates branding to all slides.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO choices improve a slide's clarity for a general audience? (Select TWO.)

options.text: One main message per slide with supporting visuals
options.rationale: Correct: a single idea aids comprehension.

options.text: Sufficient colour contrast and a limited type scale
options.rationale: Correct: contrast and restraint improve readability and accessibility.

options.text: Paragraphs of body text read aloud verbatim
options.rationale: Dense text competes with the speaker.

options.text: A different font and colour on every line

items.explanation: Correct: a single idea aids comprehension.

items.stem: A slide must let executives compare revenue across five regions precisely. Which visual is most appropriate?

options.text: A clean bar/column chart with sorted values and labels
options.rationale: Correct: bars support precise magnitude comparison.
3-D pies distort and hinder precise comparison.

options.text: A dense table in tiny font
options.rationale: A tiny table is hard to read from the room.

options.text: A decorative image with no data

items.explanation: Correct: bars support precise magnitude comparison.
